scenes.text: How does Google Photos find your dog, when you just type dog? [1] How does Spotify know which songs feel similar? [2] The answer is embeddings.

An embedding turns something, a word, a sentence, or an image, [1] into a list of numbers that captures its meaning. [2] Meaning becomes numbers. [3] Similar things end up close together. [4] It's like giving every idea a location on a map.

data.definition: A list of numbers that captures the meaning of text, images or sound.

scenes.text: Picture a map of meaning. [1] Fruits cluster together. Animals over here. Vehicles over there. [2] Now, search for puppy. [3] Its nearest neighbours are dog and cat. Not because the letters match, but because the meaning does.

data.heading: A map of meaning
data.note: Search by meaning, not by spelling

scenes.text: This is called vector search. [1] First, every document is turned into an embedding, [2] meaning a list of numbers, [3] and saved in a vector database. [4] When you search, your query becomes numbers too, [5] and the database returns the closest matches, in milliseconds.
You've already used this. [1] Google Photos finding beach, with no tags. [2] Spotify and YouTube suggesting similar songs. [3] And online stores showing, you may also like.
Myth! [1] Search just matches exact keywords. [2] Not anymore. Embedding search matches meaning. Search cheap flights, and it also finds budget airfare, with zero words in common.

data.fact: Embedding search matches meaning: “cheap flights” also finds “budget airfare”.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! In embedding space, which word sits closest to king? [1] Pause and think. <pause 3.2> [2] Queen! Similar meaning, close together. Comment queen if you got it!

Recap. [1] Embeddings turn meaning into numbers. [2] Similar things sit close together. [3] Vector databases search them by meaning. [4] They power photo search, recommendations, and more. [5] Next episode, the big one. RAG. How to make A I answer from your own documents. Follow A I Maastaaru!
